questions.stem: A client with dark skin has an SpO2 reading of 93% but has increasing shortness of breath and confusion. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Studies show pulse oximeters may overestimate saturation in people with darker skin pigmentation, which can hide hypoxemia. Clinical signs and ABGs guide decisions.

options.text: Document the normal saturation and continue to monitor
Recognize that pulse oximeters can overestimate oxygen saturation in people with darker skin, assess the client's overall condition, and anticipate an arterial blood gas
Remove the oximeter permanently
Assume the confusion is unrelated

questions.stem: After a stroke, a client understands and uses language correctly but has slurred speech that is hard to understand. How should the nurse document this?
questions.rationale: Dysarthria is a motor speech disorder caused by weakness of the muscles used for speech. Aphasia is a language disorder affecting comprehension or expression. Speech therapy approaches differ.

options.text: Expressive aphasia
Dysarthria
Receptive aphasia
Global aphasia

questions.stem: The family of a client with a newly diagnosed frontal lobe brain tumor reports recent personality changes. Which changes does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: The frontal lobe governs executive function and personality. Occipital tumors affect vision, and cerebellar tumors affect coordination. Safety and family support are important.

options.text: Loss of hearing
Impulsiveness, poor judgment, disinhibition, and changes in personality
Visual field loss only
Loss of balance only

questions.stem: An 81-year-old has weight loss, fatigue, new atrial fibrillation, and withdrawn behavior. Which condition should the nurse recognize as a possible cause?
questions.rationale: Older adults with hyperthyroidism may lack classic hyperactive symptoms and instead show apathy, weight loss, and atrial fibrillation. Thyroid testing is needed.

options.text: Normal aging
Apathetic hyperthyroidism
Myxedema
Cushing's syndrome

questions.stem: A client who has taken prednisone 15 mg daily for 2 years is scheduled for major surgery. What does the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Long-term steroid use suppresses the adrenal glands, which cannot increase cortisol during surgical stress. Stress dosing prevents adrenal crisis, which can cause refractory hypotension.

options.text: Stopping prednisone a week before surgery
Continuing the usual steroid and possibly receiving additional IV hydrocortisone (stress dosing) around surgery, as prescribed
Doubling the dose for a month after surgery
No change in steroids

questions.stem: A client had an esophagectomy with a gastric pull-up. Which nursing action is most important?
questions.rationale: Elevation reduces reflux and aspiration. The NG tube lies across a fresh anastomosis, so blind manipulation risks a leak. Signs of a leak include fever, chest pain, and tachycardia.

options.text: Keep the head of the bed flat
Keep the head of the bed elevated at least 30 degrees, and do not reposition or irrigate the NG tube without the surgeon's order
Encourage a large meal on day 1
Reinsert the NG tube if it falls out

questions.stem: A client is traveling to an area with poor sanitation. Which advice helps prevent traveler's diarrhea?
questions.rationale: Food and water precautions and hand hygiene reduce exposure to enteric pathogens. Oral rehydration is the mainstay if diarrhea occurs.

options.text: "Eat raw salads and drink tap water with ice."
"Boil it, cook it, peel it, or leave it. Drink bottled or treated water, avoid ice and street food, and wash hands often."
"Take antidiarrheal medicine every day."
"Avoid all fruit."

questions.stem: A client who had a kidney transplant 5 years ago asks why the provider recommends yearly skin checks. What is the nurse's best response?
questions.rationale: Immunosuppressed clients have much higher rates of squamous cell carcinoma and other skin cancers. Prevention and early detection are key.

options.text: "Transplant recipients have lower cancer risk."
"Long-term immunosuppression greatly increases the risk of skin cancers, so daily sun protection and regular skin exams are important."
"Skin checks are only for people over 80."
"Sunscreen isn't needed if you have darker skin."

questions.stem: A client had carpal tunnel release surgery today. Which instruction should the nurse include?
questions.rationale: Elevation reduces swelling, and finger movement prevents stiffness and tendon adhesions. Neurovascular changes may indicate tight dressings or complications.

options.text: "Keep your hand below your waist."
"Elevate your hand above heart level, move your fingers often to prevent stiffness, and report increasing numbness, swelling, or color change."
"Lift heavy objects to strengthen your wrist right away."
"Keep the dressing wet."

questions.stem: Two hours into a plasma transfusion, a client develops acute respiratory distress, hypoxemia, fever, and hypotension. There is no JVD, and BNP is normal. What does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: TRALI is noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, often with hypotension and fever. TACO typically causes hypertension, JVD, and an elevated BNP. For both, the transfusion is stopped and respiratory support given, but diuretics help TACO, not TRALI.

options.text: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO)
Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI)
A mild allergic reaction
Iron overload

questions.stem: Which lesion description is most typical of basal cell carcinoma?
questions.rationale: Basal cell carcinoma is the most common skin cancer. It rarely spreads but can invade locally. Melanoma follows the ABCDE warning signs.

options.text: An asymmetric mole with multiple colors
A pearly or waxy bump with rolled edges and small visible blood vessels, sometimes with a central ulcer
A flat, uniform brown freckle
A fluid-filled blister

questions.stem: Why should the nurse have clients remain in the clinic for about 15 minutes after receiving a vaccine?
questions.rationale: Syncope, especially in adolescents, and anaphylaxis usually occur shortly after vaccination. A longer observation period (30 minutes) is used for clients with prior allergic reactions.

options.text: To collect payment
To observe for fainting and rare immediate allergic reactions such as anaphylaxis, with emergency medications available
To check antibody levels
It is not necessary

questions.stem: A child with ADHD on a pediatric unit earns a sticker each time they complete a task, and stickers can be traded for extra playtime. What behavioral approach is this?
questions.rationale: Rewarding desired behavior increases its frequency. Token systems are effective when rewards are immediate, consistent, and meaningful to the child.

options.text: Punishment
Positive reinforcement (token economy)
Negative reinforcement
Extinction

questions.stem: A laboring client has had an epidural for 5 hours. Which assessment is especially important?
questions.rationale: A full bladder can slow fetal descent, increase discomfort, and contribute to postpartum hemorrhage. The bladder is assessed regularly and emptied as needed.

options.text: Pupil response
Bladder distention, with catheterization as needed, because the epidural can reduce the sensation and urge to void
Hearing
Deep tendon reflexes in the arms

questions.stem: An infant with an unrepaired cleft palate is having difficulty feeding. Which technique should the nurse teach the parents?
questions.rationale: A cleft palate prevents effective suction. Special feeders, upright positioning, and frequent burping reduce choking, fatigue, and air swallowing. Feedings should take no longer than about 30 minutes.

options.text: "Feed the baby lying flat."
"Use a specialized bottle and nipple for cleft palate, feed the baby in an upright position, and burp frequently because the baby swallows extra air."
"Feed only once every 6 hours."
"Use a regular bottle with a large hole cut in the nipple."

questions.stem: Highlight (circle) the findings that require immediate follow-up.
questions.rationale: A new pulmonary infiltrate with chest pain, fever, and hypoxemia in a client with sickle cell disease defines acute chest syndrome, a leading cause of death in sickle cell disease. Not using incentive spirometry is a modifiable risk factor. BP is stable.
questions.answer_summary: Chest pain with splinting; hypoxemia; fever; tachypnea; new infiltrate; hemoglobin drop; unused incentive spirometer

passage_segments.text: New chest pain with shallow breathing

questions.correct_text: Chest pain with splinting; hypoxemia; fever; tachypnea; new infiltrate; hemoglobin drop; unused incentive spirometer

questions.stem: For each item, indicate whether it is a contributing factor to acute chest syndrome or a clinical finding of it.
questions.rationale: Hypoventilation during a pain crisis causes atelectasis and hypoxia, which promote sickling in the lungs. Infection and fat embolism from bone marrow infarction are other causes.
questions.answer_summary: Contributing: shallow breathing from pain, opioid sedation, unused incentive spirometer. Findings: new infiltrate, hypoxemia, fever.

rows.text: Shallow breathing from back and chest pain
Sedation from opioids reducing deep breaths
New lobar infiltrate on chest x-ray

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.
questions.rationale: Acute chest syndrome can worsen rapidly, requiring ICU care and mechanical ventilation. The hemoglobin drop suggests hemolysis or pooling of blood in the lungs.
questions.answer_summary: 1: acute chest syndrome; 2: progressive respiratory failure
questions.template: The client has ___1___ and is at high risk for ___2___.

questions.stem: Which interventions does the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Management includes oxygenation, lung expansion, treating possible infection including atypical organisms, transfusion to improve oxygen delivery, and balanced analgesia. Excess fluids can cause pulmonary edema, and untreated pain worsens splinting.

options.text: Supplemental oxygen to reach the prescribed saturation target
Incentive spirometry every 1–2 hours while awake
Broad-spectrum antibiotics (such as ceftriaxone plus a macrolide)
Blood transfusion (simple or exchange) as prescribed
Effective pain control with monitoring of sedation and respiratory rate
Increasing IV fluids to three times maintenance
Stopping all opioid pain medication

questions.stem: Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.rationale: Hypoxemia is the most immediate threat, and hypoxia promotes further sickling. The nurse then notifies the provider and coaches incentive spirometry. Increasing opioids could worsen hypoventilation.

options.text: Apply oxygen and raise the head of the bed
Increase the morphine PCA basal rate
Obtain a sputum culture
Encourage the client to walk in the hallway

questions.stem: Forty-eight hours after treatment begins, the nurse reassesses the client. For each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or requires immediate follow-up.
questions.rationale: Improving oxygenation, infection control, lung expansion, and pain show response. Sickle cell disease raises stroke risk, so new neurological signs require emergency evaluation. Oversedation with slow breathing requires stopping opioids, airway support, and possibly naloxone.
questions.answer_summary: Improved: oxygenation, afebrile, good incentive spirometer volumes, controlled pain. Follow-up: possible stroke; opioid oversedation.

rows.text: Achieving 1,500 mL on the incentive spirometer
Sudden severe headache and slurred speech
Sedation score indicating the client is difficult to arouse, with RR 8/min

questions.stem: The nurse in an urgent care center is triaging four clients who just arrived. Which client should the nurse care for first?
questions.rationale: Alkaline chemical eye injuries penetrate quickly and can cause permanent vision loss. Immediate, prolonged irrigation is required before any other assessment.

options.text: A client who splashed drain cleaner into one eye 5 minutes ago and is in severe pain
A client with an ankle sprain from basketball
A client with a sore throat and a temperature of 100.4°F (38°C)
A client requesting a tetanus booster after a clean scrape

questions.stem: A client on telemetry has new, frequent PVCs. The client is alert with stable BP. Which labs should the nurse check first?
questions.rationale: Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia increase myocardial irritability and PVCs. Other triggers include hypoxia, ischemia, caffeine, and certain drugs.

options.text: Serum amylase and lipase
Serum potassium and magnesium
Hemoglobin A1C
Uric acid

questions.stem: A client had sclerotherapy for varicose veins today. Which instruction should the nurse include?
questions.rationale: Compression and walking promote venous flow and help the treated veins close. Heat and prolonged sitting increase the risk of clots.

options.text: "Avoid walking for a week."
"Wear the prescribed compression stockings, walk regularly, and avoid prolonged sitting, hot baths, and sun exposure to the treated areas for the time directed."
"Apply heat packs to the injection sites."
"Sit with your legs crossed."

questions.stem: An adolescent with cystic fibrosis uses a high-frequency chest wall oscillation vest. When should the nurse recommend the treatment?
questions.rationale: Airway clearance on a full stomach can cause vomiting. Bronchodilators open the airways and mucolytics thin secretions, which improves clearance. Regular daily therapy prevents mucus plugging and infection.

options.text: Right after eating a large meal
Before meals or at least 1–2 hours after eating, usually after bronchodilator inhalation, followed by hypertonic saline or dornase alfa as prescribed
Only when the client has a fever
Once a week

questions.stem: A subclavian central venous catheter was just placed. Which action is required before the nurse uses the line?
questions.rationale: Subclavian and internal jugular insertions can puncture the lung. Confirming placement and checking for pneumothorax prevents harm from infusing into the wrong place.

options.text: Flush it with a large volume of saline immediately
Confirm tip placement and rule out pneumothorax with a chest x-ray (or other approved method), and assess breath sounds and respiratory status
Start vasopressors right away
Remove the sterile dressing

questions.stem: A college student is diagnosed with meningococcal meningitis. The roommate asks what to do. What is the nurse's best response?
questions.rationale: Chemoprophylaxis with rifampin, ciprofloxacin, or ceftriaxone for close contacts reduces the risk of secondary cases. Healthcare workers need prophylaxis only after unprotected exposure to respiratory secretions.

options.text: "You don't need to do anything."
"Close contacts like roommates should receive preventive antibiotics as soon as possible, and should watch for fever, headache, or stiff neck."
"You need the live vaccine instead."
"Wait until you have symptoms."

questions.stem: A malnourished client with alcohol use disorder is confused, has an unsteady gait, and has abnormal eye movements (nystagmus). What does the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia suggest Wernicke encephalopathy, which is caused by thiamine deficiency. Prompt thiamine can reverse symptoms and prevent permanent Korsakoff syndrome.

options.text: IV dextrose first, then thiamine the next day
IV thiamine promptly, before or with glucose
Lorazepam alone
Vitamin C supplements

questions.stem: An 84-year-old with type 2 diabetes and reduced kidney function is prescribed glyburide. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Glyburide is on the Beers Criteria list because of prolonged hypoglycemia risk. Safer options are chosen, and glucose goals are individualized.

options.text: Administer it as prescribed
Clarify the prescription, because glyburide carries a high risk of prolonged hypoglycemia in older adults, especially with kidney impairment
Double the dose
Give it at bedtime without food

questions.stem: A client has taken omeprazole daily for 8 years. Which potential long-term effects should the nurse discuss with the provider?
questions.rationale: Long-term acid suppression affects nutrient absorption and gut flora. Periodic review determines whether continued therapy is needed or the dose can be reduced.

options.text: Improved bone density
Increased risk of fractures, low magnesium, low vitamin B12, and C. difficile infection
Decreased infection risk
Hyperkalemia

questions.stem: A client receiving hemodialysis asks what "dry weight" means. What is the nurse's best response?
questions.rationale: Dry weight guides how much fluid is removed each session. Weight gain between sessions reflects fluid intake, and large gains increase the risk of hypotension during dialysis and of heart strain.

options.text: "Your weight after a big meal."
"Your target weight after dialysis, when excess fluid has been removed and you have no swelling, without becoming too low in fluid."
"Your weight before dialysis."
"Your weight when you were a child."

questions.stem: A homebound older adult with little sun exposure has diffuse bone pain, muscle weakness, and a low vitamin D level. Which condition does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Vitamin D deficiency impairs bone mineralization, which softens bones and increases fracture and fall risk. Treatment is vitamin D and calcium replacement.

options.text: Gout
Osteomalacia
Osteoarthritis
Fibromyalgia

questions.stem: A 5-year-old has had increasing tiredness, pallor, frequent nosebleeds, easy bruising, and bone pain for several weeks. Which condition should the nurse recognize as a concern?
questions.rationale: Bone marrow infiltration crowds out normal cells, causing anemia, low platelets, and bone pain. A CBC with differential is the first step in evaluation.

options.text: Iron deficiency only
Acute leukemia
Growing pains
Seasonal allergies

questions.stem: A 58-year-old reports persistent bloating, feeling full quickly, and pelvic discomfort almost daily for 6 weeks. What should the nurse recommend?
questions.rationale: Ovarian cancer often causes vague, persistent symptoms. There is no reliable screening test for average-risk clients, so symptoms lasting more than 2–3 weeks warrant evaluation.

options.text: "These are normal digestive changes with age."
"Schedule an evaluation soon, because persistent symptoms like these can be early signs of ovarian cancer."
"Take antacids and wait a few months."
"Only worry if you have vaginal bleeding."

questions.stem: A client was bitten by a bat that flew into the house and has never received a rabies vaccine. Which treatment does the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear, and bat bites can be tiny. Post-exposure prophylaxis given promptly is highly effective.

options.text: No treatment unless symptoms develop
Thorough wound washing, human rabies immune globulin at the wound site, and a series of rabies vaccine doses
Antibiotics only
A single tetanus shot only

questions.stem: After a traumatic event, a client cannot remember important personal information about the event and appears detached. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Dissociation is a protective response to overwhelming trauma. Safety and gradual processing in therapy help, and pressuring recall can retraumatize the client.

options.text: Force the client to recall the event in detail immediately
Provide a safe, calm environment, use grounding techniques, avoid pushing for memories, and support referral for trauma-focused therapy
Tell the client they are faking
Leave the client alone for long periods

questions.stem: A client arrives at the emergency department after a sexual assault 3 hours ago. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Trauma-informed care supports the client's control and safety. Evidence is preserved (no showering, clothing bagged in paper) if the client consents. Care includes STI and pregnancy prophylaxis options and advocacy resources.

options.text: Encourage the client to shower before the exam
Provide a private, supportive environment, explain options, obtain consent for each step, and involve a trained sexual assault nurse examiner (SANE) if available, while preserving evidence
Question the client about why they were in that situation
Discard the client's clothing

questions.stem: A GBS-positive client in active labor asks why IV penicillin is being started now. What is the nurse's best response?
questions.rationale: Adequate intrapartum prophylaxis (at least 4 hours before delivery) prevents early-onset GBS disease in newborns. The newborn is observed after birth according to risk.

options.text: "It treats a urinary infection."
"Giving antibiotics at least 4 hours before birth greatly reduces the chance of your baby developing a serious GBS infection."
"It will speed up your labor."
"It's only needed after the baby is born."

questions.stem: During a newborn exam, the provider feels a "clunk" as the hip is gently moved outward and forward. How should the nurse interpret this finding?
questions.rationale: The Ortolani and Barlow maneuvers screen for hip instability. Unequal thigh folds and limited abduction are other signs. Early treatment, such as a Pavlik harness, gives the best results.

options.text: A normal finding in all newborns
A positive Ortolani maneuver, suggesting developmental dysplasia of the hip, which needs follow-up
A sign of a clavicle fracture
A sign of hypotonia

questions.stem: A 10-year-old has wrist pain and swelling after a fall, and the x-ray shows a fracture through the growth plate. Why is follow-up especially important?
questions.rationale: The growth plate (physis) is the weakest part of a child's bone. Salter-Harris classification guides treatment, and some injuries need surgery to protect growth.

options.text: Growth plate fractures heal slower than adult fractures in all cases
Injuries to the growth plate can disrupt bone growth, causing limb length differences or deformity, so orthopedic follow-up is needed
Children don't need casts
Growth plate injuries never need treatment

questions.stem: Highlight (circle) the findings that require immediate follow-up.
questions.rationale: These findings match serotonin toxicity. Linezolid is an MAO inhibitor, and combining it with an SSRI, tramadol, trazodone, and ondansetron greatly increases serotonin activity. The WBC reflects the pneumonia, and SpO2 is acceptable.
questions.answer_summary: Agitation/confusion; clonus with hyperreflexia; hyperthermia; tachycardia and hypertension; diarrhea and mydriasis; linezolid combined with sertraline

passage_segments.text: Linezolid started 24 hours ago while taking sertraline

questions.correct_text: Agitation/confusion; clonus with hyperreflexia; hyperthermia; tachycardia and hypertension; diarrhea and mydriasis; linezolid combined with sertraline

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it is more typical of serotonin syndrome or neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS).
questions.rationale: Both cause hyperthermia and autonomic instability, but neuromuscular findings, timing, and the causative drug help distinguish them. Treatments differ (for example, cyproheptadine for serotonin syndrome and dantrolene or bromocriptine for NMS).
questions.answer_summary: Serotonin syndrome: rapid onset, clonus and hyperreflexia, GI hyperactivity and mydriasis, tremor. NMS: lead-pipe rigidity with slowed reflexes, gradual onset after antipsychotic.

rows.text: Onset within about 24 hours of a medication change
Gradual onset over days after starting an antipsychotic
Tremor and agitation with hyperactive bowel sounds

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.
questions.rationale: The rapid onset after linezolid with classic neuromuscular signs points to serotonin toxicity rather than sepsis alone. Muscle-generated heat can rise rapidly and become life-threatening.
questions.answer_summary: 1: serotonin syndrome from interacting serotonergic drugs; 2: severe hyperthermia leading to rhabdomyolysis, seizures, and organ failure
questions.template: The client is experiencing ___1___ and is at risk for ___2___.

options: serotonin syndrome from interacting serotonergic drugs
blanks.correct: serotonin syndrome from interacting serotonergic drugs

options: severe hyperthermia leading to rhabdomyolysis, seizures, and organ failure
blanks.correct: severe hyperthermia leading to rhabdomyolysis, seizures, and organ failure

questions.stem: Which interventions does the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Treatment centers on stopping the offending drugs, sedating with benzodiazepines, using cyproheptadine, cooling, and supportive care. Restraints increase muscle activity, heat production, and lactic acidosis. Antipyretics don't work because the heat comes from muscle activity, not a change in the brain's temperature set point.

options.text: Stop all serotonergic medications (and review the choice of antibiotic)
Benzodiazepines for agitation and muscle activity
Cyproheptadine (a serotonin antagonist)
Active external cooling and IV fluids
Continuous cardiac monitoring
Physical restraints to control agitation
Acetaminophen as the main treatment for the fever

questions.stem: The client's next scheduled tramadol and sertraline doses are due. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Continuing serotonergic drugs worsens toxicity. The provider will stop them and may change the antibiotic. The nurse also reviews other contributors such as ondansetron and trazodone.

options.text: Give both doses as scheduled
Hold all serotonergic medications and notify the provider immediately
Give sertraline only
Give tramadol with extra ondansetron

questions.stem: Twenty-four hours after treatment begins, the nurse reassesses the client. For each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or requires immediate follow-up.
questions.rationale: Most serotonin syndrome resolves within 24–72 hours after stopping the offending drugs. Rhabdomyolysis requires aggressive fluids to protect the kidneys, and seizures require benzodiazepines and emergency evaluation.
questions.answer_summary: Improved: temperature, vital signs, clonus resolved, mental status. Follow-up: rhabdomyolysis; seizure.

rows.text: CK 18,000 units/L with dark, tea-colored urine

exhibits.content: pH 7.31, PaCO2 62 mm Hg, HCO3 31 mEq/L, PaO2 52 mm Hg. Previous baseline (clinic records): pH 7.37, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, HCO3 30 mEq/L.

exhibits.label: Other results
exhibits.content: WBC 15,800/mm3. Chest x-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate.

case_studies.title: Set 2: Respiratory System: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 22-year-old client is admitted to the emergency department after a motorcycle crash. The client was not wearing a helmet. EMS reports the client was unconscious for about 1 minute at the scene, then woke up and was talking.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1400
exhibits.content: Alert and oriented x4. GCS 15. Pupils 3 mm, equal, and briskly reactive. Reports headache rated 5/10. Abrasions on the right forearm. Swelling and deformity of the left wrist. BP 128/78 mm Hg, HR 88/min, RR 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air. Head CT has been ordered and is pending.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1600
exhibits.content: Increasingly drowsy. Vomited twice in 20 minutes. Opens eyes only to painful stimuli, speaks in confused sentences, and localizes to pain. Right pupil 6 mm and sluggish; left pupil 3 mm and brisk. BP 168/70 mm Hg, HR 54/min, RR 10/min and irregular, SpO2 94% on room air.

case_studies.title: Set 3: Neurological System: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 19-year-old college student with type 1 diabetes is brought to the emergency department by a roommate. The client has had vomiting and body aches for 2 days and stopped taking insulin "because I wasn't eating anything."

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 2200
exhibits.content: Lethargic but arousable and oriented. Deep, rapid respirations. Fruity odor on the breath. Dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor. Reports frequent urination and extreme thirst for 2 days. Abdominal pain rated 6/10.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 99.8°F (37.7°C), HR 124/min, RR 32/min and deep, BP 94/56 mm Hg, SpO2 99% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: glucose 486 mg/dL, arterial pH 7.18, PaCO2 24 mm Hg, HCO3 10 mEq/L, potassium 5.6 mEq/L (3.5–5.0), sodium 131 mEq/L (135–145), anion gap 24 (8–12), serum beta-hydroxybutyrate elevated, BUN 32 mg/dL (7–20), creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (0.6–1.2).

case_studies.title: Set 4: Endocrine System: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 58-year-old client with end-stage kidney disease receives hemodialysis every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The client missed Friday's session because of a family emergency and arrives at the emergency department on Monday morning.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0730
exhibits.content: Reports generalized muscle weakness, tingling in the hands and around the mouth, and shortness of breath when lying down. Crackles in both lung bases. +2 pitting edema in the lower legs. Weight is 4.2 kg above the client's documented dry weight. Anuric. Left forearm AV fistula with palpable thrill and audible bruit.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 98.2°F (36.8°C), HR 54/min and irregular, RR 24/min, BP 172/98 mm Hg, SpO2 91% on room air.

exhibits.label: Additional information
exhibits.content: 12-lead ECG: tall, peaked T waves, widened QRS complex, and flattened P waves.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: potassium 7.2 mEq/L (3.5–5.0), sodium 133 mEq/L, BUN 110 mg/dL, creatinine 11.2 mg/dL, HCO3 16 mEq/L (22–26), phosphorus 7.8 mg/dL (2.5–4.5), calcium 7.9 mg/dL (8.6–10.2), hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL.

case_studies.title: Set 5: Renal and Genitourinary System: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 62-year-old client with osteoarthritis who takes ibuprofen 800 mg three times daily is brought to the emergency department by a spouse. The client had two black, tarry stools yesterday and vomited dark material that looked like coffee grounds this morning.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1000
exhibits.content: Anxious and pale. Skin cool and clammy. Reports epigastric pain rated 5/10 and lightheadedness when standing. Capillary refill 4 seconds. Abdomen soft and nondistended.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 97.8°F (36.6°C), HR 122/min, RR 24/min, BP 88/52 mm Hg (baseline 140/80), SpO2 95% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL (12–16), hematocrit 22% (36–48), BUN 42 mg/dL (7–20), creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, platelets 240,000/mm3, INR 1.1.

case_studies.title: Set 6: Gastrointestinal System and Nutrition: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 24-year-old client sustained a closed fracture of the left femoral shaft in a motorcycle crash and is in skeletal traction awaiting surgical fixation.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, day 2 (36 hours after injury), 0600
exhibits.content: Client is newly restless and confused, asking "Where am I?" Reports difficulty breathing. Pinpoint reddish-purple spots noted across the upper chest, in both axillae, and on the conjunctivae. Left thigh is swollen, and pain at the fracture site is rated 5/10. Pin sites are clean with a small amount of clear, crusted drainage. Traction weights hang freely. Left pedal pulse is palpable, and toes are warm with brisk capillary refill.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 101.2°F (38.4°C), HR 124/min, RR 30/min, BP 118/70 mm Hg, SpO2 86% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: platelets 98,000/mm3 (on admission: 240,000/mm3), hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL.

case_studies.title: Set 7: Musculoskeletal System: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 54-year-old client with acute myeloid leukemia is on day 10 after induction chemotherapy. The client has a right upper arm peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC).

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 2000
exhibits.content: Client reports shaking chills and says, "I just don't feel right." Skin warm and flushed. Redness and tenderness about 2 cm around the PICC insertion site, without drainage. Oral mucosa has several small ulcers. Scattered petechiae on both lower legs. Gums bled slightly during mouth care. Pale and reports fatigue.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 101.5°F (38.6°C), HR 118/min, RR 24/min, BP 96/58 mm Hg (baseline 124/76), SpO2 95% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: WBC 0.6 × 10³/mm³, absolute neutrophil count (ANC) 200/mm³, hemoglobin 8.1 g/dL, platelets 22,000/mm³, lactate 2.8 mmol/L (0.5–2.0), creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (baseline 0.9).

case_studies.title: Set 8: Hematology and Oncology: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 34-year-old client is in the emergency department being treated for acute pyelonephritis. The client reports no known drug allergies. The first dose of IV ceftriaxone was started 10 minutes ago.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1510
exhibits.content: Client suddenly reports itching all over, a tight throat, and feeling faint. The nurse notes widespread raised, red hives; swelling of the lips and eyelids; a hoarse voice; and audible expiratory wheezing. The client is anxious and says, "I feel like something terrible is happening."

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 100.4°F (38°C), HR 128/min, RR 28/min, BP 78/42 mm Hg (on arrival: 122/76), SpO2 89% on room air.

case_studies.title: Set 9: Immune System and Infectious Disease: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 42-year-old client weighing 80 kg is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after being burned in a house fire. There was no enclosed-space smoke exposure; the client was burned while pulling a family member from a burning porch.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0300
exhibits.content: Alert and oriented. Voice clear; no soot in the mouth or nose; no singed nasal hair. Burns cover the entire anterior trunk and the anterior surfaces of both legs. Some areas are red, blistered, moist, and very painful; other areas are white, dry, leathery, and painless to touch. Pedal pulses palpable bilaterally. Pain rated 9/10. Indwelling urinary catheter inserted: 15 mL of dark amber urine in the first hour.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 97.0°F (36.1°C), HR 128/min, RR 24/min, BP 96/60 mm Hg, SpO2 97% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: hematocrit 54% (37–47), potassium 5.4 mEq/L (3.5–5.0), sodium 134 mEq/L (135–145).

case_studies.title: Set 10: Integumentary System and Burns: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 78-year-old client with heart failure takes furosemide 40 mg daily and digoxin 0.125 mg daily. The client has had nausea and vomiting for 3 days from viral gastroenteritis but kept taking the furosemide. The client is admitted from the emergency department.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1100
exhibits.content: Reports weakness, dizziness when standing, and leg cramps. Dry mucous membranes. Abdomen mildly distended with hypoactive bowel sounds. Voided 150 mL of dark amber urine since arrival 4 hours ago. Respirations shallow. Cardiac monitor shows sinus tachycardia with frequent premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) and prominent U waves.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 98.8°F (37.1°C). Lying: BP 108/64 mm Hg, HR 102/min. Standing: BP 86/50 mm Hg, HR 124/min, client reports near-fainting. RR 12/min. SpO2 95% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: sodium 136 mEq/L, potassium 2.6 mEq/L (3.5–5.0), chloride 88 mEq/L (98–106), magnesium 1.4 mg/dL (1.7–2.2), BUN 38 mg/dL, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (baseline 0.9). Arterial blood gas: pH 7.50, PaCO2 46 mm Hg, HCO3 34 mEq/L.

case_studies.title: Set 11: Fluids, Electrolytes, and Acid-Base Balance: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 32-year-old client, now gravida 4 para 4, gave birth vaginally 45 minutes ago to a 4,200-g (9 lb 4 oz) newborn after an 18-hour labor augmented with oxytocin. The placenta delivered intact. The oxytocin infusion was stopped after delivery of the placenta. The client has initiated breastfeeding.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1545
exhibits.content: The client reports feeling dizzy and "a gush of blood." Perineal pad saturated in 15 minutes with several large clots. Fundus boggy, 2 cm above the umbilicus, and deviated to the right. Bladder palpable above the symphysis; the client has not voided since delivery. Skin pale and cool. Quantitative blood loss since birth: 950 mL.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 118/min, BP 92/58 mm Hg (1 hour ago: 124/78), RR 22/min, SpO2 97% on room air, T 98.8°F (37.1°C).

exhibits.label: History
exhibits.content: no hypertension, no asthma. Blood type O positive.

case_studies.title: Set 12: Maternity and Newborn: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 4-month-old infant born at term is brought to the emergency department by a parent. The infant has had a runny nose and cough for 3 days. A rapid test is positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0200
exhibits.content: Parent reports the infant took only 1 oz (30 mL) of formula in the past 4 hours and has had 2 wet diapers in 12 hours. Parent also reports that at home the infant "stopped breathing for a few seconds" once. Copious thick nasal secretions. Nasal flaring, subcostal and intercostal retractions, and head bobbing. Expiratory wheezes and fine crackles bilaterally. Anterior fontanel slightly sunken. Mucous membranes dry. Capillary refill 3 seconds. Infant is irritable, alternating with periods of lethargy.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 100.9°F (38.3°C) rectal, HR 172/min, RR 68/min, SpO2 88% on room air. Weight 6.4 kg.

case_studies.title: Set 13: Pediatrics: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 52-year-old client is 2 days postoperative after open reduction and internal fixation of an ankle fracture sustained in a fall. On admission, the client reported drinking "6 to 8 beers a day" for years. The last drink was about 52 hours ago.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 2200
exhibits.content: Client is agitated, pulling at the IV, and says, "Get those bugs off the wall!" Oriented to person only. Coarse tremor of both hands. Profuse sweating. Reports nausea. Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol (CIWA-Ar) score: 22.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 100.9°F (38.3°C), HR 128/min, RR 24/min, BP 178/102 mm Hg, SpO2 96% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: glucose 68 mg/dL, magnesium 1.3 mg/dL (1.7–2.2), potassium 3.2 mEq/L (3.5–5.0), AST 142 units/L, ALT 70 units/L. A dextrose-containing IV fluid has been prescribed.

case_studies.title: Set 14: Mental Health: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 58-year-old client weighing 90 kg is admitted with an acute pulmonary embolism. The provider prescribes IV heparin per the facility's weight-based protocol. Baseline aPTT 30 seconds, platelets 230,000/mm³.

exhibits.label: Heparin protocol
exhibits.content: Bolus 80 units/kg IV, then infuse 18 units/kg/hr. Premixed bag: heparin 25,000 units in 500 mL D5W (50 units/mL). Bolus vial: heparin 5,000 units/mL. Check aPTT 6 hours after starting and 6 hours after every rate change. Adjustments by aPTT: below 45 seconds, rebolus 40 units/kg and increase by 2 units/kg/hr; 46–70 seconds (therapeutic), no change; 71–90 seconds, decrease by 2 units/kg/hr; above 90 seconds, hold the infusion for 1 hour, then decrease by 3 units/kg/hr and notify the provider.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 6 hours after starting heparin
exhibits.content: Client reports that their gums bled when brushing teeth. Urine in the bedside urinal is pink-tinged. No headache; neurologically intact. Vital signs: HR 96/min, BP 128/76 mm Hg, RR 20/min, SpO2 95% on 2 L/min nasal cannula.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: aPTT 98 seconds, platelets 210,000/mm³, hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL (baseline 13.6).

case_studies.title: Set 15: Pharmacology and Dosage Calculation: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: At 0700, an RN on a medical-surgical unit receives a five-client assignment and works with one LPN/VN and one assistive personnel (AP). Handoff report:

exhibits.label: Room 1
exhibits.content: 68-year-old, postoperative day 1 after bowel resection. Stable. Morphine PCA; pain 3/10. Needs ambulation 3 times today and scheduled oral medications.

exhibits.label: Room 2
exhibits.content: 55-year-old with COPD admitted overnight. SpO2 87% on 2 L/min nasal cannula, RR 28/min, using accessory muscles, speaking in short phrases.

exhibits.label: Room 3
exhibits.content: 80-year-old with advanced dementia. Stable. Needs feeding assistance and incontinence care. Ate 50% of dinner.

exhibits.label: Room 4
exhibits.content: 45-year-old with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes, going home this afternoon. Has not yet received insulin teaching. Fasting glucose 188 mg/dL.

exhibits.label: Room 5
exhibits.content: 72-year-old with heart failure. Stable. Weight up 0.2 kg from yesterday. Due for IV furosemide at 0900, subcutaneous enoxaparin, and oral medications. Morning potassium 3.1 mEq/L.

case_studies.title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: An 82-year-old client is on postoperative day 2 after a hip hemiarthroplasty. The client has mild cognitive impairment but lived alone independently before admission. Yesterday the client was alert and oriented x3.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0200
exhibits.content: Client is restless, pulling at the IV, and trying to climb over the raised side rails, saying, "I have to go home and feed my cat." Oriented to person only. Eyeglasses and hearing aids are in the bedside drawer. The urinary catheter was removed yesterday at 1400; the client has not voided in 8 hours, and a bladder scan shows 650 mL. Morse Fall Scale score: 85.

exhibits.label: Medications given this evening
exhibits.content: diphenhydramine 50 mg PO at 2200 (PRN for sleep) and hydromorphone 1 mg IV at 2300.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 100.6°F (38.1°C), HR 102/min, RR 20/min, BP 118/70 mm Hg, SpO2 91% on room air.

case_studies.title: Set 17: Safety and Infection Control: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 29-year-old client, gravida 2 para 1, at 31 weeks' gestation comes to labor and delivery reporting "tightening" of the abdomen and low back pain for 3 hours. She also reports burning with urination for 2 days.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1600
exhibits.content: Contractions every 5 minutes, lasting 40 seconds, palpating moderate. Sterile speculum and cervical exam: 2 cm dilated, 80% effaced; membranes intact. Fetal fibronectin: positive. Group B streptococcus status: unknown. Fetal heart rate baseline 145/min with moderate variability and accelerations; no decelerations.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 99.1°F (37.3°C), HR 92/min, RR 18/min, BP 118/72 mm Hg.

exhibits.label: Urinalysis
exhibits.content: positive nitrites and leukocyte esterase.

case_studies.title: Set 18: Mixed Review 1: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 64-year-old client with long-standing, poorly controlled hypertension arrives at the emergency department 45 minutes after the sudden onset of severe chest pain. The client describes the pain as "tearing" and says it moves through to the back between the shoulder blades.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1130
exhibits.content: Diaphoretic and anxious. Pain rated 10/10. New diastolic murmur heard at the left sternal border. Right radial pulse strong; left radial pulse weaker. Lungs clear.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: BP right arm 196/108 mm Hg, left arm 150/88 mm Hg; HR 112/min; RR 24/min; SpO2 96% on room air; T 98.4°F (36.9°C).

exhibits.label: Diagnostics
exhibits.content: 12-lead ECG shows sinus tachycardia without ST elevation. Troponin within normal limits. CT angiography: marked widening of the mediastinum; an intimal flap visible in the ascending aorta with contrast tracking within the aortic wall; small pericardial effusion; aortic regurgitation noted on cardiac views; no coronary artery occlusion.

case_studies.title: Set 19: Mixed Review 2: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 19-year-old client dove into a shallow lake and is brought to the emergency department 40 minutes later, immobilized with a cervical collar. CT shows a C6 vertebral fracture with spinal cord injury.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1500
exhibits.content: Alert and oriented x3. Weak elbow flexion bilaterally; no movement of the hands, trunk, or legs. Absent sensation below the upper chest. Breathing is shallow and mainly abdominal. Vital capacity 1.2 L (predicted 4.5 L). Skin below the injury is warm, dry, and flushed. Priapism present. Abdomen soft. Focused ultrasound (FAST) exam negative for internal bleeding.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 97.0°F (36.1°C), HR 48/min, RR 24/min, BP 78/44 mm Hg (MAP 55), SpO2 93% on 2 L/min nasal cannula.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL, lactate 1.6 mmol/L.

case_studies.title: Set 20: Mixed Review 3: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 79-year-old resident of a long-term care facility with type 2 diabetes is admitted after 3 days of decreased oral intake during a urinary tract infection. The resident takes metformin and glipizide.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0900
exhibits.content: Lethargic, disoriented to place and time. Mucous membranes dry and cracked. Poor skin turgor over the sternum. Respirations regular, not deep; no fruity breath odor. Urine dark and cloudy.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 100.8°F (38.2°C), HR 118/min, RR 20/min, BP 92/54 mm Hg, SpO2 95% on room air. Weight 64 kg.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: glucose 986 mg/dL, serum osmolality 362 mOsm/kg (275–295), sodium 149 mEq/L, potassium 4.9 mEq/L, BUN 58 mg/dL, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, arterial pH 7.36, HCO3 22 mEq/L, serum ketones trace. Urinalysis: positive nitrites and leukocytes.

case_studies.title: Set 21: Mixed Review 4: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 9-month-old infant is brought to the pediatric emergency department by a parent. The infant has had a fever for 18 hours and has become increasingly irritable and difficult to console. The infant's immunizations are behind schedule.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 2100
exhibits.content: Infant cries more when picked up and held (paradoxical irritability) and has a high-pitched cry. Anterior fontanel is bulging while the infant is calm and upright. Vomited twice. Refusing bottle; 1 wet diaper in 8 hours. A few nonblanching purple spots on the lower legs. Capillary refill 3 seconds.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 103.6°F (39.8°C) rectal, HR 176/min, RR 40/min, BP 80/44 mm Hg, SpO2 96% on room air. Weight 8.5 kg.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: WBC 22,000/mm³, blood glucose 72 mg/dL. Lumbar puncture is planned.

case_studies.title: Set 22: Mixed Review 5: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 67-year-old client arrived at the emergency department 14 hours after the onset of chest pain and was diagnosed with a large anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction. The client is awaiting emergency cardiac catheterization.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0400
exhibits.content: Newly confused and restless. Skin cool, clammy, and mottled on the knees. Crackles halfway up both lung fields. Jugular venous distention at 45°. New S3 gallop. Urine output 10 mL/hr for the past 2 hours.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 118/min, BP 78/50 mm Hg (MAP 59), RR 30/min, SpO2 88% on 4 L/min nasal cannula, T 98.0°F (36.7°C).

exhibits.label: Laboratory and diagnostic results
exhibits.content: lactate 4.2 mmol/L (0.5–2.0), creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (baseline 1.0), troponin markedly elevated. Bedside echocardiogram: left ventricular ejection fraction 20% with a large area of anterior wall akinesis.

case_studies.title: Set 23: Mixed Review 6: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 46-year-old client with a history of heavy daily alcohol use arrives at the emergency department with severe epigastric pain that began 12 hours ago and radiates to the back. The client reports nausea and has vomited several times. The last drink was 10 hours ago.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1300
exhibits.content: Pain rated 9/10, slightly relieved by sitting up and leaning forward. Abdomen distended with guarding; bowel sounds hypoactive. Mucous membranes dry. Client reports tingling around the mouth.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 100.6°F (38.1°C), HR 124/min, RR 26/min, BP 94/58 mm Hg, SpO2 93% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: lipase 2,400 units/L (0–160), glucose 248 mg/dL, calcium 7.6 mg/dL (8.6–10.2), WBC 16,800/mm³, hematocrit 50% (37–47), BUN 34 mg/dL, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (baseline 0.9), triglycerides normal.

case_studies.title: Set 24: Mixed Review 7: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 24-year-old client is brought to the emergency department by a roommate after telling friends by text that they "took a whole bottle" of extra-strength acetaminophen about 18 hours ago. The client has been vomiting since this morning.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1400
exhibits.content: Drowsy but arousable; oriented to person only. Flapping tremor of the hands when the arms are extended (asterixis). Right upper quadrant tenderness. Sclera slightly yellow. The client says, "I just wanted everything to stop."

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 99.0°F (37.2°C), HR 108/min, RR 20/min, BP 106/64 mm Hg, SpO2 97% on room air. Weight 60 kg.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: serum acetaminophen 180 mcg/mL at an estimated 18 hours after ingestion (well above the treatment line), AST 4,200 units/L, ALT 5,100 units/L, INR 3.2, total bilirubin 4.1 mg/dL, glucose 58 mg/dL, ammonia elevated, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL.

case_studies.title: Set 25: Mixed Review 8: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 38-year-old farmworker is brought to the emergency department about 1 hour after being sprayed with an organophosphate insecticide while working in a field. The client's clothing is damp and has a strong chemical odor.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1100
exhibits.content: Anxious and intermittently confused. Excessive drooling, tearing, and sweating. Vomited twice and had diarrhea and urinary incontinence. Pupils pinpoint. Visible muscle twitching in the arms and chest. Diffuse wheezing with copious, bubbling airway secretions.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 44/min, BP 92/56 mm Hg, RR 30/min, SpO2 86% on room air, T 98.8°F (37.1°C).

case_studies.title: Set 26: Mixed Review 9: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 34-year-old client with Graves' disease stopped taking methimazole 2 months ago because "I felt better." The client has had a cough and fever for 3 days and is brought in by a partner for increasing agitation.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1900
exhibits.content: Restless, agitated, and intermittently disoriented. Profuse sweating. Fine tremor of the hands. Reports several loose stools daily. Bulging eyes (exophthalmos) and a diffusely enlarged thyroid with an audible bruit. Raised, thickened skin on both shins. Crackles in the right lower lobe.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 104.9°F (40.5°C), HR 168/min and irregularly irregular (atrial fibrillation), RR 28/min, BP 150/60 mm Hg, SpO2 93% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: TSH undetectable, free T4 markedly elevated, glucose 180 mg/dL, WBC 15,200/mm³, AST and ALT mildly elevated. Chest x-ray: right lower lobe infiltrate.

case_studies.title: Set 27: Mixed Review 10: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 3-year-old is brought to the emergency department after being found face-down in a backyard pool. The estimated submersion time is about 2 minutes. A parent began rescue breathing and compressions; the child coughed up water and began breathing before EMS arrived. There was no diving or fall.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1630
exhibits.content: Drowsy but opens eyes and responds to voice. Coughing frothy, pink-tinged sputum. Crackles in both lung fields. Subcostal and intercostal retractions. Clothing wet. Skin cool and mottled on the arms and legs; shivering.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 95.0°F (35.0°C) rectal, HR 148/min, RR 44/min, BP 92/58 mm Hg, SpO2 89% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: blood glucose 160 mg/dL, sodium 138 mEq/L. Chest x-ray: patchy bilateral infiltrates.

case_studies.title: Set 28: Mixed Review 11: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 71-year-old client with atrial fibrillation stopped taking apixaban 3 weeks ago because of cost. The client arrives at the emergency department reporting sudden, severe pain in the left leg that began 2 hours ago while watching television.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 2000
exhibits.content: Left foot and lower leg are pale and cold to the touch. Left pedal and popliteal pulses absent by palpation, with no Doppler signal at the dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial arteries. Reports numbness of the left toes. Weak dorsiflexion of the left foot. Capillary refill in the left toes greater than 5 seconds. Right leg warm with palpable pulses. No leg swelling.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 112/min and irregularly irregular, BP 148/86 mm Hg, RR 20/min, SpO2 97% on room air, T 98.4°F (36.9°C).

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, potassium 4.3 mEq/L, creatine kinase 280 units/L (mildly elevated).

case_studies.title: Set 29: Mixed Review 12: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 9-year-old is admitted for abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus yesterday and moved to the right lower quadrant overnight. The child has vomited twice and refuses to eat.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0800
exhibits.content: Lying still with knees flexed. Tenderness and rebound tenderness at McBurney's point. T 101.8°F (38.8°C), HR 118/min, BP 104/66 mm Hg, RR 22/min. WBC 16,400/mm³. Ultrasound shows an enlarged, noncompressible appendix. NPO; IV fluids running. Surgery is scheduled for later this morning.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1030
exhibits.content: The child says, "My tummy suddenly feels better." Twenty minutes later, the child is lethargic, the abdomen is diffusely rigid and distended, and bowel sounds are absent. T 103.3°F (39.6°C), HR 146/min, BP 86/50 mm Hg, RR 30/min, capillary refill 4 seconds.

case_studies.title: Set 30: Mixed Review 13: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 44-year-old client is admitted with tingling in the feet that began 5 days ago and has progressed to weakness in both legs and now the hips. Two weeks ago, the client had a diarrheal illness after eating undercooked chicken.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0900
exhibits.content: Symmetric weakness of both legs (2/5) and mild weakness of both arms (4/5). Deep tendon reflexes absent in the legs and diminished in the arms. Reports aching back and leg pain. Mild difficulty swallowing thin liquids. Alert and oriented.

exhibits.label: Vital signs over the past 4 hours
exhibits.content: HR ranging from 48 to 128/min; BP ranging from 88/50 to 182/104 mm Hg; RR 22/min; SpO2 95% on room air.

exhibits.label: Respiratory measurements
exhibits.content: forced vital capacity 22 mL/kg (baseline 50 mL/kg), negative inspiratory force −26 cm H2O.

exhibits.label: Lumbar puncture
exhibits.content: elevated CSF protein with a normal white blood cell count.

case_studies.title: Set 31: Mixed Review 14: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 26-year-old client, gravida 1 para 0, at 35 weeks' gestation comes to labor and delivery reporting a severe headache that is not relieved by acetaminophen and "seeing spots."

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1400
exhibits.content: Reports pain under the right ribs. Face and hands swollen. Patellar reflexes 4+ with 3 beats of ankle clonus. Fetal heart rate baseline 140/min with moderate variability; no contractions.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: BP 172/114 mm Hg (repeated 15 minutes later: 168/112), HR 96/min, RR 18/min, SpO2 98% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 0.9 (elevated), platelets 108,000/mm³, AST 88 units/L, ALT 94 units/L, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL.

case_studies.title: Set 32: Mixed Review 15: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 58-year-old client experiencing homelessness is brought to the emergency department after being found outdoors in freezing weather, wearing wet clothing. Bystanders report the client had been drinking alcohol.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0600
exhibits.content: Lethargic and confused; responds to loud voice. Not shivering. Skin cold and pale. Fingers of both hands are white, waxy, hard, and numb. Pupils sluggish.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: core (esophageal) temperature 86°F (30°C), HR 42/min and irregular, BP 84/50 mm Hg, RR 8/min; pulse oximetry unable to obtain a reliable reading.

exhibits.label: ECG
exhibits.content: slow atrial fibrillation with prominent J (Osborn) waves.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: glucose 62 mg/dL, potassium 4.4 mEq/L, blood alcohol elevated.

case_studies.title: Set 33: Mixed Review 16: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 76-year-old client with atrial fibrillation who is not on anticoagulation (stopped because of falls) arrives at the emergency department with sudden, severe abdominal pain around the umbilicus that began 4 hours ago. The client has vomited twice and had an urgent, forceful bowel movement.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1500
exhibits.content: Pain rated 10/10; client is writhing. Abdomen soft, mildly distended, with only mild tenderness and no guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds hyperactive.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 124/min and irregularly irregular, BP 102/64 mm Hg, RR 24/min, T 99.6°F (37.6°C), SpO2 96% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: lactate 4.8 mmol/L (0.5–2.0), WBC 18,200/mm³, arterial pH 7.29, HCO3 17 mEq/L. CT angiography shows an embolus occluding the superior mesenteric artery.

case_studies.title: Set 34: Mixed Review 17: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 28-year-old client at 30 weeks' gestation is brought to labor and delivery after a car crash. She was wearing only the lap belt, positioned across the top of her abdomen. A previous ultrasound showed a fundal (upper uterine) placenta.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1600
exhibits.content: Reports severe, constant abdominal pain. Moderate dark red vaginal bleeding. Uterus rigid, tender, and does not relax between frequent small contractions. Fetal heart rate baseline 170/min with minimal variability and recurrent late decelerations.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 120/min, BP 96/58 mm Hg (prenatal baseline 118/74), RR 24/min, SpO2 97% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, platelets 110,000/mm³, fibrinogen 150 mg/dL (normal in pregnancy about 300–600), blood type O negative.

case_studies.title: Set 35: Mixed Review 18: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 19-year-old client with Burkitt lymphoma began induction chemotherapy 30 hours ago. The client received IV fluids and allopurinol before chemotherapy.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0800
exhibits.content: Reports nausea, fatigue, muscle cramps, tingling around the mouth, and a "fluttering" feeling in the chest. Urine output 20 mL/hr for the past 3 hours. Positive Chvostek's sign.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 110/min with frequent PVCs, BP 150/90 mm Hg, RR 20/min, SpO2 97% on room air, T 98.8°F (37.1°C).

exhibits.label: Additional information
exhibits.content: 12-lead ECG: peaked T waves.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: potassium 6.6 mEq/L, phosphorus 8.9 mg/dL (2.5–4.5), calcium 6.8 mg/dL (8.6–10.2), uric acid 14.2 mg/dL (3.5–7.2), creatinine 2.3 mg/dL (baseline 0.8), BUN 45 mg/dL. G6PD status: not yet documented.

case_studies.title: Set 36: Mixed Review 19: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 3-year-old is admitted with a fever of 103–104°F (39.4–40°C) for 6 days that has not responded to acetaminophen or ibuprofen.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1000
exhibits.content: Very irritable and difficult to console. Both eyes red without drainage. Lips red, dry, and cracked, with a bright red "strawberry" tongue. Blotchy red rash on the trunk. Hands and feet swollen and red. A single enlarged, tender lymph node (2 cm) on the right side of the neck. Lungs clear. Capillary refill 2 seconds.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 103.8°F (39.9°C), HR 156/min, RR 30/min, BP 96/60 mm Hg. Weight 14 kg.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: C-reactive protein and ESR markedly elevated, platelets 520,000/mm³, albumin 2.8 g/dL, ALT mildly elevated, urinalysis with sterile pyuria. Echocardiogram is scheduled.

case_studies.title: Set 37: Mixed Review 20: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 34-year-old client with epilepsy ran out of levetiracetam 4 days ago. The client is brought to the emergency department by EMS after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that began at home.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 2210
exhibits.content: The client has had continuous generalized tonic-clonic activity for 7 minutes (including prehospital time) without regaining consciousness between convulsions. Gurgling respirations with frothy, blood-tinged oral secretions from a bitten tongue. Urinary incontinence. No IV access yet.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: HR 136/min, BP 172/100 mm Hg, RR 28/min and irregular, SpO2 86% on room air, T 101.0°F (38.3°C).

exhibits.label: Point-of-care results
exhibits.content: glucose 58 mg/dL, sodium 136 mEq/L.

case_studies.title: Set 38: Mixed Review 21: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 17-year-old with sickle cell disease (HbSS) was admitted 2 days ago with a vaso-occlusive crisis causing back and leg pain. The client has a morphine PCA and IV fluids. The incentive spirometer at the bedside has not been used.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 0400
exhibits.content: New right-sided chest pain that worsens with breathing, and a cough. Breathing is shallow, and the client is guarding the chest. Crackles in the right lower lobe. Drowsy but arousable.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 102.2°F (39°C), HR 124/min, RR 30/min, BP 112/66 mm Hg, SpO2 89% on room air.

exhibits.label: Laboratory and imaging results
exhibits.content: hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL (baseline 8.5), WBC 19,000/mm³, reticulocytes elevated. Chest x-ray shows a new right lower lobe infiltrate.

case_studies.title: Set 39: Mixed Review 22: unfolding case study

case_studies.scenario: A 52-year-old client who takes sertraline 150 mg daily and trazodone at bedtime was admitted with MRSA pneumonia. IV linezolid was started 24 hours ago. The client has also received tramadol for pleuritic pain and IV ondansetron for nausea.

exhibits.label: Nurses' notes, 1400
exhibits.content: Agitated, restless, and intermittently confused. Profuse sweating. Tremor of both hands. Hyperactive reflexes in the legs with sustained ankle clonus. Pupils dilated. Three episodes of diarrhea since noon. Muscle tone increased in the legs more than the arms.

exhibits.label: Vital signs
exhibits.content: T 103.1°F (39.5°C), HR 132/min, BP 168/98 mm Hg, RR 24/min, SpO2 95% on 2 L/min.

exhibits.label: Laboratory results
exhibits.content: CK 1,900 units/L (mildly elevated), creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, WBC 13,800/mm³.

case_studies.title: Set 40: Mixed Review 23 (Final Set): unfolding case study
